svg.title: What msb pause stops, and what keeps running
svg.desc: A sandbox's host process (msb machine) holds a microVM with one vCPU, two job processes (a busy loop and a progress counter) and guest memory, plus host-side tasks: relay, metrics, clock sync, network. On msb pause, input is held, the jobs freeze, the vCPU stops and the counter holds at 217, while memory stays in RAM, the host tasks keep running and host CPU drops from about 100% to about 2.5%. A new exec sent while paused is turned away by the relay: sandbox is paused; resume it before starting guest work. On msb resume, the clock is fixed, the vCPU starts, the jobs thaw, input flows again and the counter carries on at 218.
svg.text: What pause stops, and what keeps running

g.text: Running. The vCPU is busy and the job’s counter ticks.
Pause. Hold input, freeze the jobs, stop the vCPU. Memory and the host side stay.
Resume. Fix the clock, start the vCPU, thaw the jobs, let input through.
